pack.title: Rogue generic fault-code descriptions
pack.source: Original descriptions written for Rogue OBD2 Diagnostic Tool. Generic interpretations; manufacturers may define codes differently.

definitions.description: Camshaft timing actuator (intake, bank 1): control circuit fault
inspection: Check solenoid resistance against specification
Inspect wiring and connector
Command the solenoid with a scan tool if supported and listen for a click

definitions.description: Camshaft timing (intake, bank 1): too far advanced or system performance fault
causes: Sticking timing solenoid or blocked oil screen
Worn timing chain or stretched chain
inspection: Check oil level, grade and condition first
Inspect the timing solenoid and its oil screen
Compare desired and actual cam angle in Live Data if available
Check timing chain stretch (crank/cam correlation)
repairs: Change oil to the correct grade
Clean or replace the timing solenoid
Replace the timing chain or cam phaser if worn

definitions.description: Oxygen sensor heater (bank 1, sensor 1): control circuit fault
causes: Failed heater element inside the oxygen sensor
Blown fuse for the heater supply
symptoms: Longer time to reach closed-loop fuel control
Possible slight increase in fuel use
inspection: Check the heater fuse
Measure heater resistance at the sensor (typically a few ohms; see service manual)
Check for battery voltage on the heater supply with ignition on
Inspect wiring near the exhaust for melting
repairs: Replace the oxygen sensor if the heater is open

definitions.description: Manifold pressure / mass air flow does not agree with throttle position
causes: Vacuum or intake air leak after the MAF sensor
inspection: Check for intake leaks (smoke test)
Compare MAF, MAP and throttle readings in Live Data
Inspect throttle body for carbon build-up

definitions.description: Fuel rail or system pressure too low
causes: On diesels: air in fuel or worn high-pressure pump
symptoms: Hesitation or loss of power under load
inspection: Compare desired and actual rail pressure in Live Data
Check fuel filter service history
Test fuel pump supply pressure and volume with a gauge
Check pump power and ground
repairs: Replace fuel pump or high-pressure pump

definitions.description: Fuel rail or system pressure too high
causes: Faulty fuel pressure regulator or control valve
inspection: Compare desired and actual rail pressure
Check the pressure sensor signal against a mechanical gauge
Inspect the pressure control valve and its wiring
repairs: Replace pressure regulator or control valve

definitions.description: Fuel system leak detected: large leak
causes: External fuel leak from lines, injector seals or rail
Faulty pressure sensor giving false reading
inspection: Stop the engine and check for fuel leaks before running it again
Inspect high-pressure lines and fittings
Check injector leak-off where applicable

definitions.description: Mass air flow (MAF) sensor: circuit fault
causes: Open or shorted wiring to the mass air flow sensor
inspection: Inspect the connector for corrosion, bent pins and poor locking
Check the wiring harness for chafing, heat damage or rodent damage
With a multimeter, check supply voltage, ground and signal at the sensor connector against the service manual values
Clear the code and confirm whether it returns
repairs: Replace the mass air flow sensor if it fails testing

definitions.description: Mass air flow (MAF) sensor reading out of expected range
causes: Air leak between MAF and throttle
inspection: Inspect air filter and intake ducting for leaks or cracks
Compare MAF g/s at idle with engine size (roughly 2-4 g/s per litre at warm idle is typical)
Clean the sensor with MAF-safe cleaner only

definitions.description: Coolant takes too long to reach the temperature needed for closed-loop fuel control
symptoms: Slow warm-up and weak cabin heat
inspection: Check coolant level
Watch coolant temperature in Live Data during warm-up
Feel the upper radiator hose: it should stay cool until the thermostat opens

definitions.description: Coolant temperature stays below the thermostat's regulating temperature
causes: Thermostat stuck open or opening too early
Cooling fan running all the time
inspection: Monitor coolant temperature in Live Data on a drive: it should reach normal operating temperature
Check whether the cooling fan runs when the engine is cold
repairs: Replace coolant temperature sensor if it reads incorrectly

definitions.description: Oxygen sensor bank 1 sensor 1: circuit fault
symptoms: Possible poor fuel economy or rough running
inspection: Watch the sensor voltage in Live Data: a warm upstream narrow-band sensor normally switches between about 0.1 and 0.9 V
Check for exhaust leaks ahead of the sensor
Inspect wiring and connector
Check fuel trims for a lean or rich condition
repairs: Fix any lean/rich condition or exhaust leak first
Replace the oxygen sensor if it is slow or dead
